notes: Official local government websites by Census code: counties by 5-digit county GEOID, towns and townships (county subdivisions with an active government) by state code + 5-digit COUSUB, and incorporated places by 7-digit place GEOID. Sources: the U.S. Census Bureau's 2022 Government Units listing (WEB_ADDRESS, self-reported, public domain: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/gus/datasets/2022/govt_units_2022.ZIP) and Wikidata's official website (P856, CC0) by FIPS code (P882, P774); the Census address wins when both qualify. Each site was opened on 2026-10-15 and kept only when it is the government's own live site: it answered over https, the page names that government, and its title is not a parked, for-sale, spam, chamber of commerce, tourism, travel or real-estate page; or it is a .gov site (or a site the government reported to Census under its own name) that turns automated visitors away. Thirteen of the largest cities and counties whose listed sites were dead or missing use their sites as opened in a browser that day. Counties Census lists without a government (Connecticut planning regions, Rhode Island counties, Alaska census areas) have none. Query strings are dropped. These are links to each government's own site, not officials. Domains lapse and get taken over, so recheck these sites before relying on an old copy.
